answer: HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): In the Barcelona province, the plant-introduction type most influenced by urban land use was UNINTENTIONAL (accidental) introductions, followed by a weaker positive influence on GARDENING (horticultural) introductions, while AGRIFOREST (agriculture/forestry) introductions were NOT influenced by urban land use. At the plot level (632 plots), Unintentional introductions showed the strongest and most consistent positive association with urban cover: raw Spearman r≈0.50, and in a negative-binomial count model accounting for cropland, elevation, climate and distances, their expected count rose ~53% per +1 SD of urban cover (IRR=1.53, 95%CI 1.27–1.85, p<1e-5) — significant at every buffer size (50/500/1000 m) and year (2009/1993/1956) tested, and robust when the 65 plots classified as "Urban" habitat were excluded (IRR=1.39, p=0.003). Gardening introductions showed a positive but weaker and less consistent urban association (raw r≈0.40; IRR≈1.20, p=0.078 overall, turning significant only when Urban-classified plots were excluded, IRR=1.21, p=0.045). AgriForest introductions showed no significant urban association in any specification (raw r≈0.11; IRR 0.73–1.11 across buffers/years, all non-significant; at most a weak tie to cropland). The urban land-use signal is carried largely by the "Urban" habitat class (adding habitat as a fixed effect absorbs the between-habitat component and all pathway effects become non-significant), but it is a genuine landscape gradient and not a classification artifact, since it persists among the 567 non-Urban plots for Unintentional introductions. Current urban cover (2009), not the historical 1956→2009 urbanization increment, is what predicts counts. Supporting context: although Gardening is the numerically dominant pathway in recent decades (75% of 1985–2019 introductions in Catalonia vs 19% Unintentional), the Unintentional pathway is the one most spatially tied to urban land use, and Unintentional species are also the most successful invaders (mean 9.6 invaded plots vs 3.9 for Gardening and 2.3 for AgriForest).

payload.hypothesis: Unintentional (accidental) plant introductions were the introduction type most influenced by urban land use (strongest, most consistent positive plot-level association with urban cover: IRR≈1.53 per +1 SD, p<1e-5), with a weaker positive influence on Gardening (horticultural) introductions, and no influence on AgriForest (agriculture/forestry) introductions; the urban signal is carried by the Urban habitat class but persists as a landscape gradient outside urban-classified plots.
payload.workflow: Load invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plot-level records, zero missingness). Outcome: per-plot counts of species per pathway (n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo/n.total). Primary predictor: urban.2009.500m (z-scored, IRR per +1 SD), with cropland, elevation, annual temperature/rainfall/radiation, distance-to-road and distance-to-stream controls. Negative-binomial (NB2) count models per pathway; sensitivity: (i) with habitat as fixed effect, (ii) excluding the 65 Urban-habitat plots, (iii) urbanization increment (urban.2009−urban.1956), (iv) buffer/year robustness (50/1000 m; 1993/1956), and raw Spearman correlations. Context: chi-square on temporal_trends_contingency_table pathway×period; species-level trait means per pathway from invasion_success_pathways.csv; tree tip-label matching. Pathway ranking by urban IRR/significance produced the hypothesis.
